corrected_proposal.title: April 2025 Trump Administration Plan Proposed Cutting the CDC Budget by More Than 40%
corrected_proposal.description_short: CNN reported an April 10 internal plan proposed a CDC budget reduction of more than 40%; the draft could change and was not an enacted cut.
corrected_proposal.description_medium: An internal federal health-agency document dated April 10, 2025, proposed reducing the CDC budget by more than 40%, CNN reported on April 16. CNN said the draft could still be finalized with changes and would consolidate health programs into a proposed Administration for a Healthy America. This corrected card concerns a proposal, not a March cut already in effect or proof that every surveillance program named in the original synopsis ended.
corrected_proposal.description_long: CNN reported on April 16, 2025, that an internal Trump administration document dated April 10 outlined a proposed reduction of more than 40% in the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s budget. The document also previewed a broader restructuring of federal health agencies and consolidation of programs into a proposed Administration for a Healthy America. CNN reported that the plan could still be finalized with changes and described the reductions as what would happen “if enacted as is.” The evidence supports a proposed budget action; it does not show that the CDC had already received a 40% reduction in March. Nor does the accessed reporting substantiate that every program named in the original synopsis—including outbreak-detection grants, chronic-disease programs, global surveillance across 49 countries, and state emergency-preparedness agreements—was eliminated by this same proposal. This card therefore focuses on the April 10 proposal and leaves implementation unresolved. It does not combine the proposal, agency layoffs, and program closures into one completed event. The percentage is CNN’s description of the administration’s plan, not a final appropriation or an independently audited spending change.
organization_tags: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

This corrected card keeps the sourced health-agency layoffs that included NIH, gives the date and figure at the agency-wide scope supported by reporting, and drops the unsupported NIH-only details.
